Right-click the .zip file and select 'Extract All'
Choose a destination folder and click 'Extract'
Download the .zip file to your computer

questions.explanation: You cannot reliably run installers from *within* a compressed folder. You must fully extract the contents to a normal folder first.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to resolve an issue where your PC has no sound.

draggableItems.content: Ensure the application (like YouTube) isn't muted internally
Check the physical speaker connections and power
Verify the Windows volume icon in the taskbar is not muted and is turned up
Click the volume icon and verify the correct 'Playback Device' (e.g., Speakers vs Headphones) is selected

questions.explanation: Always start with physical hardware, move to OS master volume, check the specific app, and finally verify Windows is sending audio to the correct output device.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to fix a 'No Internet, Secured' Wi-Fi error on a Windows laptop.

draggableItems.content: Power cycle the router and modem
Disconnect from the Wi-Fi network and reconnect
Verify if other devices (like a phone) can access the internet on the same Wi-Fi
Run the built-in Windows Network Troubleshooter

questions.explanation: First isolate the issue: is it just the laptop or the whole network? Then try a quick reconnect, let Windows try to fix it automatically, and finally reboot the hardware.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to properly uninstall an old graphics driver and install a new one.

draggableItems.content: Restart your computer
Run the installer for the newly downloaded driver
Download the latest correct driver from the manufacturer (NVIDIA/AMD)
Uninstall the current driver using Device Manager or official removal tool

questions.explanation: You must download the new driver while you still have a stable display. Then remove the old one, reboot to clear the registry, and install the clean new driver.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to troubleshoot a smartphone app that keeps crashing instantly upon opening.

draggableItems.content: Check the App Store/Google Play Store to see if an update is available for the app
Restart the smartphone
Uninstall the app completely and reinstall it from the app store
Force close the app from the recent apps menu

questions.explanation: Start with the least destructive option: force close, then check for patches, reboot the OS, and finally wipe and reinstall the app data entirely.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to log into your router's administrative dashboard to change the Wi-Fi password.

draggableItems.content: Enter the router's admin username and password (found on the back sticker)
Find your router's Default Gateway IP address (e.g., 192.168.1.1)
Navigate to the 'Wireless' or 'WLAN' settings to change the password
Type that IP address into the address bar of a web browser

questions.explanation: Routers host a local web page for configuration. You must find its local IP, navigate to it in a browser, authenticate, and then modify settings.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to safely install a browser extension (add-on) in Google Chrome.

draggableItems.content: Read the permissions the extension is requesting before agreeing
Click 'Add to Chrome'
Navigate to the official Chrome Web Store
Search for the desired extension and verify its reviews and developer

questions.explanation: Extensions can read your web traffic, so you must use the official store, verify authenticity, and carefully read the permissions it demands.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to check if a slow PC is caused by a lack of available RAM (Memory).

draggableItems.content: Sort the list by the 'Memory' column to see which app is using the most
Click 'More details' if Task Manager opens in the simplified view
Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager
Look at the percentage at the top of the Memory column (if it's near 100%, RAM is full)

questions.explanation: Task Manager's advanced view allows you to see total system resource utilization and then sort to find the specific culprit.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to release and renew your IP address using the Windows Command Prompt (fixing an IP conflict).

draggableItems.content: Type 'ipconfig /renew' and press Enter to request a new IP
Type 'cmd' in the Start menu to open the Command Prompt
Wait for the command to finish and display your new network details
Type 'ipconfig /release' and press Enter to drop the current IP

questions.explanation: You must open the terminal, drop your current lease from the router, and explicitly ask the router's DHCP server for a fresh IP lease.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to install an application on a Mac (.dmg file).

draggableItems.content: Double-click the downloaded .dmg file to mount the virtual disk
Drag the application icon into the 'Applications' folder shortcut
Eject the virtual .dmg disk from your desktop once finished
Wait for the copy process to finish

questions.explanation: macOS often uses disk images (.dmg). Installing usually just involves dragging the executable bundle into the system Applications folder, then ejecting the installer.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to resolve a 'Blue Screen of Death' (BSOD) that just occurred on Windows.

draggableItems.content: Search the exact error code online (using a phone) to find the root cause
Take a photo of the screen with your phone, specifically noting the 'Stop Code' at the bottom
Wait for the PC to gather crash data and restart itself automatically
Do not turn off the PC immediately; let it finish writing the memory dump

questions.explanation: A BSOD writes crash logs before rebooting. Capturing the specific Stop Code is vital, as it tells you exactly what hardware or driver failed.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to physically install a new Wi-Fi router for your home.

draggableItems.content: Connect the router to power and turn it on
Use a phone or laptop to connect to the router's default Wi-Fi network and follow the setup wizard
Plug an Ethernet cable from your ISP's Modem into the 'WAN' or 'Internet' port on the router
Turn off your ISP's Modem temporarily

questions.explanation: It's best to power down the modem first to clear MAC address bindings, connect the new hardware, boot it up, and then configure the new local network.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to update the firmware on a peripheral device (like a gaming mouse or keyboard).

draggableItems.content: Click 'Update Firmware' in the software settings
Do absolutely nothing and do not unplug the device while the progress bar fills
Download and install the manufacturer's official management software (e.g., Logitech G HUB, Razer Synapse)
Ensure the device is plugged directly into the PC via USB (not wireless)

questions.explanation: Firmware flashes the internal memory of the hardware. It must be a stable wired connection, and any interruption during the flash can permanently 'brick' the device.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to boot Windows into 'Safe Mode' to remove a stubborn virus.

draggableItems.content: Navigate to Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Settings and click Restart
Press the number '4' or 'F4' to boot into Safe Mode when the menu appears
Hold the Shift key while clicking 'Restart' from the Start Menu power options
Run your antivirus scan in this minimal environment

questions.explanation: Holding Shift during restart triggers the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE). Safe mode only loads essential drivers, preventing malware from launching and defending itself.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to clear a jammed print queue in Windows.

draggableItems.content: Go to Windows Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers & scanners
Select the stuck document and choose 'Cancel' or select 'Cancel All Documents'
Click on your printer and select 'Open print queue'
Restart the printer to clear its physical memory buffer

questions.explanation: If a print job fails, it blocks all subsequent jobs. You must clear the digital queue in Windows, then restart the hardware to clear the physical cache.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to forget a Wi-Fi network on an iPhone so it stops auto-connecting to it.

draggableItems.content: Tap 'Forget This Network' at the top
Tap the blue 'i' (information) icon next to the network name
Open the Settings app and tap 'Wi-Fi'
Confirm by tapping 'Forget' in the pop-up prompt

questions.explanation: Forgetting a network deletes the saved password and stops the phone from automatically joining it in the future.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to install an app from the Google Play Store on Android.

draggableItems.content: Tap the 'Install' button and wait for the download to finish
Open the Google Play Store app
Use the search bar to find the specific app
Review the app's rating and developer to ensure it isn't a fake clone

questions.explanation: Because app stores contain many knock-off apps, it's crucial to verify the developer and reviews before hitting the install button.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to deal with a laptop that has completely frozen and won't respond to the mouse or Ctrl+Alt+Del.

draggableItems.content: Hold down the physical power button for 10-15 seconds
Wait 30 seconds for the hardware to reset
Press the power button normally to turn the laptop back on
Wait for the screen to go black and the fan/lights to turn off completely

questions.explanation: A 'Hard Power Down' is the last resort when the OS kernel panics or locks up entirely. Holding the power button cuts power at the hardware level.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to troubleshoot an external hard drive that isn't showing up in Windows.

draggableItems.content: Listen/feel if the drive is physically spinning or receiving power
Check 'Disk Management' to see if Windows detects the drive but simply hasn't assigned it a Drive Letter
Unplug the drive and try a different USB port directly on the motherboard
Try plugging the drive into a completely different computer to rule out a dead drive

questions.explanation: Start with power, then physical connection, then check if the OS sees it at a low level (Disk Management), and finally isolate the hardware by testing another PC.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to use a smartphone as a Mobile Hotspot (sharing its cellular data with a laptop).

draggableItems.content: Toggle the switch to turn the Hotspot 'On'
Go into the phone's settings and find 'Personal Hotspot' or 'Mobile Hotspot'
Set a strong, custom Wi-Fi password in the hotspot settings
On the laptop, search for the phone's Wi-Fi network and enter the password

questions.explanation: Always configure the password *before* turning the hotspot on to prevent strangers from immediately connecting and draining your data plan.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to install a custom font on Windows.

draggableItems.content: Double-click the .ttf or .otf file to open the font preview window
Download the font file (.zip) and extract it
Click the 'Install' button at the top of the preview window
Restart your applications (like Word or Photoshop) so they load the new font

questions.explanation: Fonts must be extracted, previewed, and installed into the OS registry. Applications usually cache fonts at startup, requiring a restart of the app to see the new font.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to free up space on a critically full Windows 'C:' drive.

draggableItems.content: Empty the Recycle Bin
Run the built-in 'Disk Cleanup' utility to clear temporary system files
Uninstall large video games or applications you no longer use
Check your 'Downloads' folder for large, unneeded installer files and delete them

questions.explanation: Start with the easiest wins (Recycle bin, old downloads), move to automated temp files, and finally resort to removing installed applications to reclaim gigabytes.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to troubleshoot a website that looks broken or has outdated text.

draggableItems.content: Try opening the website in 'Incognito' or 'Private' mode
Perform a 'Hard Refresh' (Ctrl + F5) to bypass the local cache
If it works in Incognito, clear your browser cache and cookies
Click the normal refresh button

questions.explanation: A hard refresh forces the browser to re-download the page. Incognito mode isolates the issue from your extensions/cookies, diagnosing a corrupted local cache.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to connect to a hidden Wi-Fi network.

draggableItems.content: Manually type in the exact network name (SSID)
Go to your Wi-Fi settings and select 'Add Network' or 'Hidden Network'
Enter the network password and click Connect
Select the correct security type (e.g., WPA2-Personal)

questions.explanation: Hidden networks do not broadcast their name. You must explicitly provide the exact SSID, define the encryption type, and supply the password.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to safely update the BIOS/UEFI on a motherboard.

draggableItems.content: Extract the firmware file and copy it to a blank USB flash drive
Download the exact BIOS update file for your specific motherboard model from the manufacturer
Restart the PC, enter the BIOS menu, and select the 'Flash' or 'Update' tool
Wait for the process to complete WITHOUT interrupting power, as a failure will permanently brick the board

questions.explanation: BIOS updates are high-risk. You must ensure exact model matching, use a stable USB drive, and never interrupt the flash process.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to resolve a 'No Bootable Device Found' error when turning on a PC.

draggableItems.content: Ensure no non-bootable USB drives are plugged into the computer
Restart the computer and enter the BIOS/UEFI settings (pressing F2 or Del)
Save changes, exit the BIOS, and let the PC restart
Check the 'Boot Order' menu to ensure your primary Hard Drive/SSD is listed first

questions.explanation: Often, a PC tries to boot from a plugged-in USB drive. If that isn't it, you must check the BIOS to ensure the internal drive hasn't been demoted in the boot order.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to test a suspect laptop battery.

draggableItems.content: Unplug the laptop from the wall charger
Generate a 'Battery Report' using Command Prompt (powercfg /batteryreport) to check health
Observe if the laptop immediately shuts off or the battery drains drastically in minutes
Ensure the laptop is turned on and indicates a 100% charge

questions.explanation: First, test if the battery holds *any* charge under load. If it doesn't shut off instantly but drains fast, run a software diagnostic report to see total degradation.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to check your internet connection speed.

draggableItems.content: Review your Download, Upload, and Ping (Latency) results
Ensure nobody else in the house is heavily downloading or streaming
Open a web browser and go to a site like Speedtest.net
Click the big 'GO' button and wait for the test to complete

questions.explanation: A speed test is only accurate if your local network is clear of heavy traffic during the test.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to set a new web browser (like Firefox) as your Default Browser in Windows.

draggableItems.content: Open Windows Settings and go to 'Apps'
Download and install the new browser
Select the new browser from the list to assign it to web protocols (HTTP/HTTPS)
Click on 'Default apps' and search for 'Web browser'

questions.explanation: You must install the software first, then use the OS 'Default apps' menu to intercept all web links and route them to the new application.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to fix a Bluetooth device that frequently disconnects from a laptop.

draggableItems.content: Put the device back into pairing mode and reconnect it to the laptop
Check if the device simply has a low battery and needs charging
Remove/Forget the device from the laptop's Bluetooth settings
Turn the laptop's Bluetooth off and back on

questions.explanation: Always rule out battery issues first. Then toggle the radio, and if issues persist, completely rebuild the pairing profile.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to fix a flickering PC monitor.

draggableItems.content: Update your graphics card drivers
Check the refresh rate in Windows Display Settings (ensure it matches the monitor, e.g., 60Hz or 144Hz)
Test the monitor on a different computer to rule out a dying screen
Ensure the video cable (HDMI/DisplayPort) is securely plugged in at both ends

questions.explanation: Start with the physical cable, then check simple OS settings (refresh rate), move to software drivers, and finally isolate the hardware.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to share a specific folder on a Windows home network.

draggableItems.content: Right-click the folder and select 'Properties'
Check the box for 'Share this folder'
Click 'Permissions' to specify who can read or write to the folder
Go to the 'Sharing' tab and click 'Advanced Sharing'

questions.explanation: Folder sharing is configured through the properties menu. Advanced sharing allows you to set the share name and explicitly define access permissions.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to reinstall Windows completely from a USB drive (Clean Install).

draggableItems.content: Boot the PC from the USB drive via the BIOS/Boot Menu
Back up all your important personal files to an external drive
Follow the Windows setup wizard, choosing to delete the old partitions and install fresh
Use the 'Windows Media Creation Tool' to create a bootable USB drive

questions.explanation: A clean install wipes everything. Backups are mandatory. Then you create the installation media, boot from it, and erase the old system drive.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to troubleshoot a microphone that isn't picking up your voice in a Zoom call.

draggableItems.content: Go to Zoom's Audio Settings and verify the correct microphone is selected
Test the microphone in the Windows Sound settings to see if the OS detects audio
Ensure you are not physically muted on the headset or digitally muted in Zoom
Ensure Windows Privacy settings are allowing desktop apps to access the microphone

questions.explanation: Check simple mutes first, then app settings, then OS level detection, and finally OS privacy permissions which can silently block mic access.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to fix a stuck/unresponsive key on a mechanical keyboard.

draggableItems.content: Use a keycap puller to gently remove the plastic keycap
Unplug the keyboard from the computer
Use compressed air to blow out any crumbs or dust from the switch mechanism
Press the bare switch to see if it moves smoothly before replacing the keycap

questions.explanation: Always unplug hardware before cleaning. Removing the keycap allows access to the mechanical switch beneath to clear out physical obstructions.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to diagnose high 'ping' (lag) while playing an online game.

draggableItems.content: Check if someone else in the house is streaming 4K video or downloading large files
Switch from Wi-Fi to a wired Ethernet cable connection
Ensure you are connected to the game server geographically closest to you
Verify if the lag is happening in all games or just one specific game

questions.explanation: Isolate the issue first (is it server specific?), check server location, rule out local network congestion, and finally upgrade the physical connection medium.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to stop an annoying program from opening automatically every time you start Windows.

draggableItems.content: Click the 'Startup' tab (or 'Startup apps' on the left side)
Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager
Restart your PC to verify the program no longer launches automatically
Right-click the offending program and select 'Disable'

questions.explanation: The Task Manager provides a dedicated 'Startup' tab to easily manage and disable programs that have registered to launch during the boot sequence.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to deal with a liquid spill on a laptop.

draggableItems.content: Turn the laptop upside down in a tent shape to let liquid drain away from the motherboard
Unplug the charger immediately
Hold the power button to force a shutdown immediately (do not take time to save files)
Leave it to dry for at least 48 hours before even attempting to turn it back on

questions.explanation: Electricity + liquid kills electronics instantly. You must cut all power sources immediately, drain the fluid, and allow extreme drying time.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to use System Restore on Windows to undo a bad driver update.

draggableItems.content: Search for 'Create a restore point' in the Start menu and open it
Select a restore point date from *before* the problem started
Wait for Windows to revert the system files and reboot
Click the 'System Restore...' button

questions.explanation: System Restore rolls back the registry and system files to a previous snapshot, effectively undoing recent software changes without affecting personal documents.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to securely connect a smart TV to your home network.

draggableItems.content: Enter the Wi-Fi password using the TV remote
Select your home Wi-Fi network (SSID) from the list
Navigate to the TV's 'Network' or 'Connections' settings menu
Allow the TV to run a connection test to verify internet access

questions.explanation: Smart devices require navigating their proprietary menus to find the network list, authenticate, and then verify the handshake with a test.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to properly install a new stick of RAM into a desktop computer.

draggableItems.content: Unplug the PC from the wall and press the power button to discharge remaining electricity
Push the RAM stick straight down firmly until the side clips snap into place
Boot the PC and check the BIOS or Task Manager to ensure the new memory is recognized
Line up the notch on the bottom of the RAM stick with the ridge in the motherboard slot

questions.explanation: Safety and static discharge first. RAM is keyed to only fit one way. It requires significant pressure to seat properly before testing.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to determine what is taking up so much space on your Mac's hard drive.

draggableItems.content: Click on 'Storage' to see a visual bar graph of usage by category
Click 'Manage...' to see recommendations and delete large files or applications
Click 'About This Mac'
Click the Apple Logo in the top-left corner

questions.explanation: macOS has a built-in storage management utility located in the 'About This Mac' system overview, which categorizes data and helps clear clutter.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to fix a mouse cursor that is moving erratically on a laptop.

draggableItems.content: Ensure the bottom of the external mouse is free of dust/hair around the sensor
If using a touchpad, clean the surface with a microfiber cloth
Try a different USB port or replace the mouse battery
Ensure you don't have a second mouse (or a game controller) plugged in and resting upside down

questions.explanation: Conflicting inputs are a common cause of erratic cursors. Afterwards, address physical obstructions on the sensors before troubleshooting ports or batteries.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to manually restart Windows Explorer when the taskbar disappears or freezes.

draggableItems.content: Click 'Restart' (or right-click and select Restart)
Scroll down the 'Processes' tab to find 'Windows Explorer' (folder icon)
Wait for the taskbar and desktop icons to vanish and reappear instantly
Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager

questions.explanation: Windows Explorer is the process responsible for the desktop UI. Restarting it via Task Manager fixes graphical glitches without needing a full PC reboot.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of a typical Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) login using an Authenticator app.

draggableItems.content: Type the 6-digit code into the website's verification prompt
Enter your username and password into the website login screen
Open the Authenticator app on your smartphone to view the current code
Wait to be prompted for your 2FA verification code

questions.explanation: 2FA requires you to successfully provide 'something you know' (your password) before it asks for 'something you have' (the time-sensitive code on your phone).

questions.question: Arrange the steps to securely set up a new account using a Password Manager.

draggableItems.content: Paste the generated password into the website's registration form
Tell the Password Manager to generate a completely random, 20-character password
Save the new login entry inside your encrypted Password Manager vault
Open your Password Manager and click 'Create New Login'

questions.explanation: You should rely on the manager to generate a complex string, use it for the site, and then save it immediately so you don't lose access.

questions.question: Arrange the emergency steps you should take immediately after accidentally clicking a suspicious link in a phishing email.

draggableItems.content: Run a full system antivirus/anti-malware scan
Disconnect your computer from the Wi-Fi or unplug the Ethernet cable to sever the connection
Change the passwords for your critical accounts (email, banking) using a DIFFERENT, safe device
Realize the website looks suspicious and close the browser tab immediately

questions.explanation: Close the threat first, then isolate the machine from the internet to prevent malware from 'phoning home' or stealing data, then scan for infections, and finally secure your external accounts from a clean device.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to set up 2FA for the very first time on a new online account.

draggableItems.content: Use your phone's authenticator app to scan the QR code displayed on the screen
Navigate to the Security settings of the website and select 'Enable 2FA'
Enter the 6-digit code the app generates back into the website to confirm it's working
Safely store the provided 'Backup Recovery Codes' offline in case you lose your phone

questions.explanation: You initiate the setup, pair the app via QR code, prove the pairing worked by entering the first code, and finally secure your backup access methods.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to create a strong, memorable 'Passphrase' (a modern alternative to complex passwords).

draggableItems.content: Combine them into one long string (e.g., 'BlueCoffeeMountainGuitar')
Think of four random, unrelated dictionary words
Check that the total length is at least 15-20 characters long
Optionally add a number or symbol at the end if the website strictly requires it

questions.explanation: Passphrases rely on extreme length rather than extreme complexity. Four random words are mathematically very secure against brute-force attacks and much easier for humans to remember.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to take if you realize you just typed your password into a fake (phishing) login page.

draggableItems.content: Enable 2FA on the account immediately if it isn't already
Log into the REAL, official website immediately
Change your password to lock out the attackers before they can use the stolen credential
Check the account settings to ensure the hackers didn't add forwarding rules or backup emails

questions.explanation: Speed is critical. You must beat the attacker to the real site, change the password to invalidate the stolen one, check for backdoors they might have installed, and harden the account with 2FA.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to log in using a physical Hardware Security Key (like a YubiKey).

draggableItems.content: Enter your username and password on the site
Wait for the website to prompt you to insert your security key
Tap the flashing gold sensor on the key to physically authorize the login
Plug the USB security key into your computer's USB port

questions.explanation: Hardware keys are the strongest form of 2FA. They require a physical presence (tapping the sensor) to prove a human is at the keyboard, not a remote hacker.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to safely handle a 'Password Expiry' prompt from your corporate IT department.

draggableItems.content: Type your current old password once to authorize the change
Receive a legitimate notification that your password will expire in 3 days
Type a completely new, unique password twice to confirm it
Ensure you update the new password on your mobile devices (like your phone's email app) so it doesn't get locked out

questions.explanation: When changing passwords, you must first prove you know the current one. Afterwards, it is crucial to update connected devices, as they will continually try the old password and lock your account.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to take if your credit card info was potentially stolen by a malicious link.

draggableItems.content: Contact the fraud department to cancel the compromised card entirely
Review your recent statement for any unauthorized charges
Call your bank or credit card provider immediately using the phone number on the back of the card
Request a new card with a completely different number to be mailed to you

questions.explanation: If payment info is compromised, you must speak directly with the bank to freeze the specific card number, dispute bad charges, and get a new credential issued.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of an 'Authenticator Push Notification' login flow (e.g., Duo, Okta Verify).

draggableItems.content: Wait for a push notification to appear on your smartphone
Tap 'Approve' or 'Yes, it's me' on the phone screen
Observe the computer screen automatically complete the login process
Type your username and password into the website

questions.explanation: Push notifications are a more convenient form of 2FA. Instead of typing a code, you simply tap 'Approve' on an out-of-band device (your phone).

questions.question: Arrange the steps to take if you receive an unexpected 2FA login code on your phone when you are NOT trying to log in.

draggableItems.content: Log into the real service immediately (since your 2FA successfully blocked them)
Change the account password, because the attacker clearly knows your current one
Do NOT share the code with anyone who might text or call asking for it
Look at the unexpected code notification and realize someone is trying to hack your account

questions.explanation: An unexpected 2FA code means a hacker correctly guessed your password but was stopped by the second factor. You must never share the code, and you must change the compromised password immediately.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to check if your email address has been compromised in a data breach.

draggableItems.content: Type your email address into the search bar
Go to a reputable security site like 'Have I Been Pwned' (haveibeenpwned.com)
Review the list of breached services to see where your data was leaked
Change your password on those specific breached services immediately

questions.explanation: HIBP securely cross-references your email against known databases of stolen credentials. If found, you must assume the password used on that specific site is public knowledge.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to recover an account if you lost your phone and cannot access your Authenticator app.

draggableItems.content: Log into the account using the backup code instead of the app code
Disable the old 2FA setup in the security settings to revoke access from the lost phone
Find the printed/saved 'Backup Recovery Codes' you secured when you first set up 2FA
Attempt to log into the website and select 'Try another way' when asked for the 2FA code

questions.explanation: Backup codes are single-use emergency bypasses explicitly designed for lost-device scenarios. Once inside, you must invalidate the old phone's access.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to deal with a 'Ransomware' warning screen that suddenly takes over your computer after clicking a bad link.

draggableItems.content: Contact IT or a security professional to assess the damage
Do NOT attempt to pay the ransom or call the phone number on the screen
Unplug the computer from the network to prevent the ransomware from spreading to other PCs
Wipe the system entirely and restore files from an offline backup (if available)

questions.explanation: Never negotiate with ransomware attackers. Isolate the machine instantly to save the rest of the network, bring in experts, and rely on offline backups to restore data.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to properly secure your home Wi-Fi password.

draggableItems.content: Log into your router's administrative dashboard
Save the settings and let the router reboot to apply the new security
Change the default password to a strong, unique passphrase
Navigate to the Wireless Security settings and ensure WPA2 or WPA3 encryption is selected

questions.explanation: You must use strong encryption protocols (WPA2/3) in addition to a strong password to prevent attackers from decrypting your Wi-Fi traffic.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to report a suspicious phishing email in a corporate environment.

draggableItems.content: Wait for IT to confirm if it was safe or malicious before interacting with it
Select the suspicious email in your inbox without opening attachments or clicking links
Use the 'Report Phishing' button (or forward the email to your IT security team)
Delete the email from your inbox once IT confirms it is malicious

questions.explanation: Reporting an email allows IT to analyze the threat and potentially delete it from all other employees' inboxes simultaneously.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of an SMS (Text Message) Two-Factor Authentication login.

draggableItems.content: Wait for a text message (SMS) to arrive on your smartphone
Type the numeric code from the text message into the website
Provide your username and password on the login screen
The website verifies the code and grants you access

questions.explanation: SMS is the most common, though slightly less secure, form of 2FA. The server texts you a temporary code after you supply the correct password.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to create a 'Salted' password for a specific website (if you don't use a password manager).

draggableItems.content: Choose a strong base passphrase that you memorize (e.g., 'BlueCoffeeMountain')
Use the combined string ('BlueCoffeeMountainAmz!') as your unique password
Add a specific identifier for the website to the end (e.g., 'Amz!' for Amazon)
Change the identifier when signing up for a different site (e.g., 'BlueCoffeeMountainNflx!')

questions.explanation: A manual 'salt' or 'modifier' system ensures you never reuse the exact same password across multiple sites, limiting the damage if one site is breached.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to take if you suspect your computer has a Keylogger installed.

draggableItems.content: Run a deep anti-malware scan using a trusted tool like Malwarebytes
Change all important passwords from a completely different, uninfected computer or phone
Stop typing any sensitive information (passwords, credit cards) on the infected machine immediately
Do not log back into any accounts on the infected PC until the malware is confirmed removed

questions.explanation: Keyloggers record every keystroke. You must stop typing immediately, secure your accounts from a safe device, and then sanitize the compromised machine.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of using 'Sign in with Google/Apple' (OAuth) on a third-party website.

draggableItems.content: Review the permissions the third-party site is requesting (e.g., 'Access your email address')
Click 'Allow' or 'Continue' to authorize the login
Click the 'Sign in with Google' button on the third-party website
You are redirected to a secure Google login page to authenticate

questions.explanation: OAuth allows you to log into a site without creating a new password. The third-party site never sees your password; it only receives an authorization token from Google/Apple.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to properly secure your smartphone physically.

draggableItems.content: Set a lock screen timeout (e.g., 30 seconds of inactivity)
Enable Biometrics (FaceID or Fingerprint) for convenience
Set a strong 6-digit PIN or alphanumeric passcode as the fallback
Ensure 'Find My Phone' or remote wipe features are turned on

questions.explanation: The PIN is the root of device security. Biometrics sit on top of the PIN. Auto-lock ensures the PIN is required quickly, and remote wipe is the final defense against theft.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to deal with a 'Browser Hijacker' (when your homepage/search engine mysteriously changes).

draggableItems.content: Open your browser's extension/add-on manager
Change your default search engine and homepage back to your preferred choice
Identify and remove any extensions you don't recognize or didn't explicitly install
Run an anti-malware scan to ensure no hidden software is forcing the changes

questions.explanation: Hijackers usually hide as rogue extensions. You must rip out the root cause before reverting the settings, then scan to ensure nothing persists in the OS.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to securely send a highly sensitive file (like a tax return) via email.

draggableItems.content: Attach the encrypted ZIP or PDF file to your email and send it
Encrypt the file or put it in a password-protected ZIP archive
Send the password to the recipient via a COMPLETELY different method (like a text message or phone call)
Never send the password in the same email as the file

questions.explanation: If a hacker intercepts the email, they get both the file and the password if sent together. Out-of-band password transmission is critical for security.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to perform a 'Security Checkup' on your Google/Microsoft account.

draggableItems.content: Go to the 'Security' or 'Account Settings' dashboard
Review the 'Recent Activity' or 'Signed-in Devices' list
Log into your main account
Click 'Sign out' or 'Revoke access' on any old phones or unrecognized computers

questions.explanation: Regularly auditing which devices have active login tokens prevents old, sold, or stolen devices from silently accessing your data.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of an Email-based Two-Factor Authentication login.

draggableItems.content: Keep the login tab open and open your email inbox in a separate tab or on your phone
Type your username and password into the website
Find the automated email containing the verification code
Type the code back into the original login tab

questions.explanation: Email 2FA relies on the assumption that only you have access to your inbox. You must check your mail out-of-band and supply the code back to the session.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to handle a fake 'Tech Support' pop-up claiming your PC is infected with a virus.

draggableItems.content: Do NOT call the phone number displayed on the screen
Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager and force close the browser
Realize it is just a deceptive website attempting to scare you into a scam
Avoid clicking 'Cancel' or the 'X' inside the webpage, as it might download malware

questions.explanation: Browser lock-screens are just scary images. Never interact with the page or call the number; use OS-level controls (Task Manager) to kill the browser.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to freeze your credit (a major step after severe identity theft).

draggableItems.content: Gather your Social Security Number and identity documents
Navigate to the official websites of the three major bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion)
Request a 'Security Freeze' to block any new credit accounts from being opened
Save the specific PINs they give you, which are required to unfreeze the credit later

questions.explanation: A credit freeze stops identity thieves from opening loans in your name. It must be done at all three bureaus individually, and the unfreeze PINs are critical.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to evaluate the safety of a shortened link (like bit.ly) before clicking it.

draggableItems.content: Notice a shortened URL in an email or social media post
Review the expanded URL to see if it points to a legitimate website or a scam site
Copy the link (do not click it) and paste it into a URL expander service (like expandurl.net)
Only click the link if the true destination is verified safe

questions.explanation: Shortened links hide their final destination. Using an expander service reveals the true URL without triggering any malicious scripts or tracking pixels.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of a 'Password Spraying' attack from a hacker's perspective (to understand how it works).

draggableItems.content: The hacker tries the password 'Winter2024!' on the first username
The hacker obtains a list of hundreds of valid employee usernames
They move to the next username and try 'Winter2024!' again, avoiding account lockouts
They successfully breach the one employee who happened to use that weak password

questions.explanation: Instead of trying many passwords on one account (which triggers lockouts), hackers try one common password across many accounts. This is why unique passwords are vital.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to properly secure your computer before walking away from it in a public space (like a library or cafe).

draggableItems.content: Press Windows Key + L (or Cmd + Ctrl + Q on Mac) to instantly lock the screen
Verify the screen requires a password to re-enter
Ensure you have all physical items (wallet, phone) on your person
Close sensitive documents or banking tabs

questions.explanation: Always hide sensitive info first, engage the OS-level screen lock, verify it engaged properly, and take physical valuables with you.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to deal with a 'You have won a gift card!' pop-up scam.

draggableItems.content: Do not click any buttons on the page, not even 'No thanks'
Close the entire browser tab using the X on the tab itself
Recognize that legitimate websites do not randomly give away expensive electronics
Clear your browser cache if the pop-ups persist on other sites

questions.explanation: Scam pop-ups often use fake 'Close' buttons that actually trigger malware downloads. The safest action is closing the tab at the browser level.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to verify if a website login page is legitimate before typing your password.

draggableItems.content: Click the padlock to ensure the security certificate belongs to the actual company (e.g., PayPal Inc.)
Only type your password if the domain and certificate are an exact match
Look at the browser address bar to verify the exact domain spelling (e.g., paypal.com, not paypa1.com)
Ensure the URL starts with 'https://' indicating a secure, encrypted connection

questions.explanation: Encryption (HTTPS) alone doesn't mean a site is safe; it just means the connection to the fake site is secure. You must verify the exact domain name and the certificate owner.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to use 'Biometric Passkeys' (the passwordless future) to log into a website on your phone.

draggableItems.content: The cryptographic key validates the login instantly without a password
Type your username into the website
The website prompts your phone's biometric sensor
Scan your fingerprint or face (FaceID) to authorize

questions.explanation: Passkeys replace passwords entirely with cryptographic tokens unlocked locally by your biometric data, making them immune to phishing.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to spot and handle a 'Smishing' (SMS Phishing) text message.

draggableItems.content: Do not click the link or reply 'STOP' to the text
Block the sender's number on your phone
Receive a text claiming a package delivery failed and requires a small fee
Go independently to the official shipping website (FedEx/UPS) to check your real tracking number

questions.explanation: Package delivery scams are the most common form of Smishing. Replying 'STOP' only confirms to the scammer that your number is active. Verify independently.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to handle a 'Credential Stuffing' attack notice (when someone tries to log into your account hundreds of times).

draggableItems.content: Log into the account (the site may require a password reset or CAPTCHA)
Enable Two-Factor Authentication to block future automated attempts
Change the password to a completely new, generated string
Receive an alert from a website that your account is 'Locked due to too many failed login attempts'

questions.explanation: A lockout means the attacker doesn't have the password but is brute-forcing it. You must secure the account by changing the password and adding a second factor.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to securely dispose of an old computer.

draggableItems.content: Take the computer or the destroyed drive to an electronics recycling center
Back up all personal files to a new computer or external drive
Use a specialized software tool (like DBAN) to completely wipe the hard drive with random data
Sign out of all software accounts (like iTunes or Adobe) and deauthorize the computer

questions.explanation: Emptying the recycle bin is not enough. You must deauthorize software licenses, cryptographically wipe the drive (or physically destroy it), and recycle the hardware.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of a 'Man-in-the-Middle' (MitM) attack on a public Wi-Fi network (to understand the risk).

draggableItems.content: You connect to 'Free Airport Wi-Fi', which is actually broadcast by the hacker's laptop
The hacker's laptop quietly intercepts and logs your password before passing it along
You open a browser and type your banking password
The bank logs you in, and you never realize your password was stolen en route

questions.explanation: MitM attacks work by secretly routing your traffic through a malicious device. This is why using a VPN on public Wi-Fi is essential to encrypt the traffic *before* it reaches the hacker.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to set up a 'Recovery Email' on your main account.

draggableItems.content: Enter a secondary email address that you have secure access to
Open the verification email sent to the secondary address and click confirm
Navigate to the Security settings of your primary email account
Select 'Add Recovery Email' or 'Account Recovery Options'

questions.explanation: A recovery email is crucial if you forget your password. You must verify ownership of the secondary address before the system will allow it to reset your primary account.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to safely open a suspicious document sent by a coworker.

draggableItems.content: Notice the email language sounds urgent or out of character for the coworker
If confirmed legitimate, proceed to open the file
Do NOT open the attached Word document
Call or message the coworker on a different platform (like Slack or phone) to ask if they actually sent it

questions.explanation: Hackers often compromise an employee's account and use it to send malware to their contacts. Out-of-band verification is the only way to ensure the sender is actually your coworker.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of what happens when you use a 'Login with Facebook' button, and why it poses a risk.

draggableItems.content: If your Facebook account gets hacked, the hacker now has instant access to that third-party site as well
Facebook passes an authentication token confirming your identity
The third-party site grants you an account without a dedicated password
You click 'Sign in with Facebook' on a random website

questions.explanation: Single Sign-On (SSO) is convenient, but it creates a single point of failure. If the central identity provider (Facebook/Google) is breached, all connected accounts fall instantly.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to manage a 'Compromised Password' alert from your iPhone or Google Chrome.

draggableItems.content: Change the password to a strong, unique string
Review the list of saved passwords that have been found in known data breaches
Click the alert to open your device's Password Manager settings
Click the link next to the compromised account to go to that website's password reset page

questions.explanation: Modern OS password managers actively scan your saved passwords against the dark web. If alerted, you must systematically go to each affected site and update the credential.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to deal with a 'Spear Phishing' email (a highly targeted attack).

draggableItems.content: Identify the 'red flag': the email asks you to purchase gift cards or wire money quickly
Receive an email that perfectly impersonates your CEO, using their name and signature
Report the email to IT and delete it
Check the sender's actual email address, revealing it is slightly misspelled (e.g., @company-inc.com instead of @company.com)

questions.explanation: Spear phishing relies on urgency and authority. Verifying the sender's actual domain name is the quickest way to unmask the attacker.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to safely read a QR code found on a public poster or parking meter.

draggableItems.content: Point your phone camera at the QR code, but do NOT tap the link immediately
Only tap to proceed if the domain name is correct and expected
Inspect the physical poster to ensure a malicious QR sticker wasn't placed over the original one
Read the preview text of the URL that your camera app displays on the screen

questions.explanation: Scammers place fake QR code stickers on parking meters to route victims to fake payment sites. Always inspect the physical code and verify the URL preview.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to configure an 'App Password' (required for old software that doesn't support modern 2FA).

draggableItems.content: Copy the 16-character generated password
Paste the generated password into the old software instead of your real password
Navigate to the Security settings of your Google/Microsoft account and select 'App Passwords'
Generate a new App Password and give it a name (e.g., 'Old Outlook on PC')

questions.explanation: App passwords are single-use, randomly generated tokens that allow legacy software to log in without triggering a 2FA prompt, keeping your main password safe.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to handle a 'Browser Notification' spam attack (constant pop-ups in the bottom right corner).

draggableItems.content: Toggle the permission from 'Allow' to 'Block' or 'Remove'
Locate the suspicious website in the 'Allowed to send notifications' list
Open your Browser Settings and navigate to 'Privacy and Security' > 'Site Settings' > 'Notifications'
Realize you accidentally clicked 'Allow' on a website prompt asking to show notifications

questions.explanation: Fake virus popups are often just abused browser notifications. You must dive into the browser's site settings to revoke the permission from the offending site.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to ensure a downloaded file isn't hiding its true, malicious extension.

draggableItems.content: Notice the file now looks like 'Invoice.pdf.exe'
Open File Explorer in Windows and go to the 'View' tab
Check the box for 'File name extensions'
Delete the malicious executable file instead of opening it

questions.explanation: Hackers name files 'Invoice.pdf.exe'. By default, Windows hides the '.exe', making it look like a harmless PDF. Enabling file extensions reveals the trick.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to deal with an unknown USB drive you found in a parking lot.

draggableItems.content: Leave the drive alone or throw it in the trash
Realize that USB drives can be engineered to fry your motherboard or automatically install keyloggers
Pick up the USB drive
Resist the urge to plug it into your computer to see what's on it

questions.explanation: Dropping malicious USB drives ('Baiting') is a common tactic to breach corporate networks. Never plug untrusted hardware into your machine.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to properly secure a Zoom or video conference meeting.

draggableItems.content: Ensure a Meeting Password/Passcode is required to join
Manually admit recognized attendees from the Waiting Room into the meeting
Generate a unique Meeting ID rather than using your Personal Meeting Room
Enable the 'Waiting Room' feature in the meeting settings

questions.explanation: To prevent 'Zoombombing', you must use unique IDs, mandate passwords, and use a Waiting Room to manually vet participants before granting them access.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how a 'Session Hijacking' (Cookie Theft) attack bypasses 2FA.

draggableItems.content: The hacker copies that cookie, puts it in their own browser, and bypasses the login screen entirely
Malware on your computer steals the 'Session Cookie' from your browser's memory
You log into a website normally, successfully completing the 2FA prompt
The website places a 'Session Cookie' on your computer so you don't have to log in again for 30 days

questions.explanation: Session cookies act as VIP passes after you log in. If malware steals the cookie, the hacker doesn't need your password or your 2FA code to access the account.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to properly lock down your social media privacy settings.

draggableItems.content: Navigate to the Privacy Settings menu
Limit past public posts to 'Friends Only'
Log into your Facebook/Instagram account
Change 'Who can see your future posts' from Public to Friends

questions.explanation: Social media defaults to public. You must navigate to settings to secure both future content and explicitly lock down historical content that attackers use to profile you.

questions.question: Arrange the broad steps of how a web page loads after you type a URL (like google.com) and press Enter.

draggableItems.content: Your browser sends an HTTP request to that specific IP address
The server at that IP address sends back the website's HTML, CSS, and image files
Your browser connects to a DNS server to translate 'google.com' into a numeric IP address
Your browser reads the code and visually renders the web page on your screen

questions.explanation: The browser first needs the IP address (DNS). Then it requests the data, receives the files from the host server, and finally translates that code into a visual interface.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of the journey of an email from the sender to the receiver.

draggableItems.content: The sender's mail server routes the message across the internet to the recipient's mail server (MTA)
The sender hits 'Send' in their email client (like Outlook or Gmail)
The recipient's server stores the email in their specific inbox
The recipient opens their email app, which downloads or syncs the message via IMAP/POP3

questions.explanation: You compose the email, your server sends it to their server, their server holds it, and their email client fetches it when they log in.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to properly implement the '3-2-1 Backup Rule' for critical data.

draggableItems.content: Save one set of backups on a different media format (like an external hard drive)
Have 3 total copies of your data (1 primary working copy, 2 backups)
Keep 1 backup off-site entirely (like in the Cloud or a physical safe deposit box)
Regularly test the backups to ensure the files can actually be restored

questions.explanation: The 3-2-1 rule means 3 copies, on 2 different media types, with 1 copy off-site. Testing them is the final, crucial step to ensure the system works.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of a DNS (Domain Name System) lookup process.

draggableItems.content: Your computer checks its own local cache to see if it already knows the IP address
The DNS server searches its records and finds the matching IP address
Your computer asks your ISP's DNS resolver for the IP address of the website
The IP address is returned to your computer so it can establish a connection

questions.explanation: The OS always checks locally first to save time. If it doesn't know, it asks the wider internet (DNS servers), gets the number, and then connects.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how an email attachment is processed.

draggableItems.content: The recipient clicks on the attachment to view or download it
The sender selects a file from their hard drive to attach
The recipient's email client decodes the text back into a usable file
The sender's email client encodes the binary file into text (MIME/Base64) so it can travel via email protocols

questions.explanation: Email was originally designed only for text. Attachments must be mathematically converted into long strings of text (encoded), sent, and then converted back (decoded) by the receiver.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of establishing a secure HTTPS connection (the 'TLS Handshake').

draggableItems.content: The client and server generate a unique, shared 'session key' for this specific visit
The client browser asks the server to identify itself
All further data sent between the browser and server is encrypted using that session key
The server responds by sending a copy of its SSL/TLS certificate

questions.explanation: The browser demands ID, the server provides its digital certificate, they agree on a temporary encryption key, and then secure communication begins.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to perform a full system backup to an external hard drive.

draggableItems.content: Click 'Start Backup' and wait for the large transfer to complete
Open the OS backup utility (like Time Machine on Mac or File History on Windows)
Select the external drive as the target destination
Plug the external hard drive into an available USB port

questions.explanation: You must physically connect the media, launch the software, tell the software where to put the data, and execute the copy.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how a browser uses a cache to speed up web browsing.

draggableItems.content: The browser skips downloading the logo and loads it instantly from the local hard drive
You visit a website for the very first time
You visit the same website three days later
The browser downloads the site's logo and saves a copy to your computer's hidden 'cache' folder

questions.explanation: Caching involves saving static assets (like images) during the first visit so subsequent visits don't waste time and bandwidth re-downloading them.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to recover a permanently deleted file using a Cloud Backup service (like Backblaze or Carbonite).

draggableItems.content: Realize you accidentally deleted an important document and emptied the recycle bin
Download the restored file back to your local computer
Log into your cloud backup account via a web browser
Navigate to the date before the deletion and locate the file in the cloud interface

questions.explanation: Cloud backups keep historical versions of your drive. You must log in, 'go back in time' to before the mistake, and pull the data back down.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of a typical e-commerce transaction processing on a web server.

draggableItems.content: The user clicks 'Submit Order'
The web server contacts a third-party payment gateway (like Stripe or PayPal) to authorize the card
The web server records the order in its database and updates inventory
The payment gateway approves the charge

questions.explanation: The order is submitted, the server asks the bank/gateway for money, the money is approved, and finally, the server updates its own records to fulfill the order.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of an email bouncing back as 'Undeliverable'.

draggableItems.content: The receiving server realizes the email address does not exist
You send an email to a misspelled address (e.g., john@gmial.com instead of gmail.com)
Your email client displays a 'Message Delivery Failure' notification in your inbox
The receiving server rejects the message and sends an automated error report back to your server

questions.explanation: You send it, the receiving server attempts to place it in an inbox but fails, it issues a rejection notice (bounce), and your server delivers that notice to you.

questions.question: Arrange the sequence of how a web browser renders HTML and CSS.

draggableItems.content: The browser reads the HTML code line-by-line to understand the structure (paragraphs, headers)
The browser applies the CSS rules (colors, fonts, layouts) to the HTML structure
The browser finally 'paints' the complete, styled page onto your computer monitor
The browser requests and downloads the raw HTML and CSS text files from the server

questions.explanation: Download the raw text, build the structural 'skeleton' (HTML), apply the 'skin/paint' (CSS), and display the final result.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of an automated cloud backup (like Google Drive desktop or OneDrive).

draggableItems.content: The file is successfully mirrored on the cloud server, safe from local hardware failure
You create and save a new Word document in your designated 'Sync' folder
The background sync application notices a new file was created
The application automatically begins uploading a copy of the file to the internet

questions.explanation: You save locally, the software detects the change, uploads it silently, and achieves parity between local and cloud.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to clear your browser cache when a website isn't loading correctly.

draggableItems.content: Select 'Cached images and files' (you can usually uncheck Passwords to stay logged in)
Open your browser's settings or history menu and find 'Clear browsing data'
Click 'Clear Data' and wait for the process to finish
Refresh the broken webpage to force it to download fresh, uncorrupted files

questions.explanation: Find the tool, select exactly what to delete (cache), delete it, and then reload the site so it has to fetch brand-new files from the server.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how a search engine (like Google) provides answers to your query.

draggableItems.content: You type a search query into the search bar
Google presents a ranked list of links on the Search Engine Results Page (SERP)
Months prior, Google's 'Spiders' crawl the internet and index billions of web pages
Google's algorithm scans its massive index to find the most relevant matches to your query

questions.explanation: Search engines don't search the live internet; they search a copy they made earlier. The crawling happens first, then you search, the algorithm ranks the offline copy, and delivers results.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to create a manual 'Disk Image' backup (a clone of your entire computer).

draggableItems.content: The software copies the operating system, settings, and all files into a single, massive image file
Connect an external hard drive that is larger than your computer's internal storage
Open disk cloning software (like Macrium Reflect or Clonezilla)
Select your 'C: Drive' as the source and the external drive as the destination

questions.explanation: A disk image is an exact 1:1 replica. You need a large drive, the right software, proper source/destination selection, and a long time to copy.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how a spam filter handles an incoming email.

draggableItems.content: The algorithm scores the email based on sender reputation and suspicious keywords
If the score is too high (suspicious), the email is routed to your Spam/Junk folder
An incoming email arrives at your email provider's server (e.g., Google's servers)
The provider's automated spam filter algorithm scans the headers, links, and content

questions.explanation: The email hits the server, gets scanned, receives a mathematical 'spam score', and is conditionally routed to the inbox or junk based on that score.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of a typical video streaming buffer (e.g., Netflix).

draggableItems.content: The video player requests a chunk of the movie from the streaming server
The server sends the video data to your device, where it sits in temporary memory (the buffer)
The player begins showing the video on your screen by reading from the buffer
As you watch, the player continuously requests the *next* chunks of video before you need them

questions.explanation: Streaming downloads data just ahead of what you are currently watching. It requests data, stores it in a buffer, plays from the buffer, and keeps refilling it.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to use an 'Unsubscribe' link safely in a legitimate email.

draggableItems.content: Scroll to the very bottom of the email to find the fine print
Click the small 'Unsubscribe' or 'Manage Preferences' link
Verify that the email is from a legitimate company you actually do business with (not a scam)
Confirm your choice on the resulting webpage to be removed from the mailing list

questions.explanation: You must verify the sender is legitimate first, because clicking 'unsubscribe' in a spam email just confirms your address is active. Then find the link, click it, and confirm.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of a 'Differential' backup routine.

draggableItems.content: On Monday, a 'Full Backup' runs, copying every single file on the computer
On Tuesday, the differential backup copies ONLY files that changed since Monday
On Wednesday, the differential backup copies files that changed on BOTH Tuesday and Wednesday
To restore the computer on Thursday, you only need Monday's full backup and Wednesday's differential file

questions.explanation: Differential backups always compare against the last FULL backup. They grow in size each day, but make restoration easy because you only ever need two files (the full, and the latest differential).

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how a '404 Page Not Found' error occurs.

draggableItems.content: Your browser successfully connects to the website's server
The server searches its directories for that specific file path
You click a link or type a URL that points to a specific article (e.g., site.com/old-news)
The server realizes the file was deleted or moved, and returns a '404 Error' message instead of the article

questions.explanation: A 404 means the internet and the server are working fine, but the specific document you asked for is gone. The server explicitly replies to tell you it cannot find the file.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of using BCC (Blind Carbon Copy) in an email.

draggableItems.content: Put your own email (or the primary recipient) in the 'To:' field
Put the list of 50 client email addresses into the 'BCC:' field
Click 'Send' to dispatch the message
Each client receives the email, but they cannot see the email addresses of the other 49 people

questions.explanation: BCC hides recipients from one another, protecting privacy when sending mass emails. You usually put yourself in the 'To' field as a placeholder.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of an 'Incremental' backup routine.

draggableItems.content: On Tuesday, the incremental backup copies ONLY files that changed since Monday
On Wednesday, the incremental backup copies ONLY files that changed since Tuesday
On Monday, a 'Full Backup' runs, copying every single file
To restore the computer on Thursday, you must load Monday's full backup, then Tuesday's file, then Wednesday's file in order

questions.explanation: Incremental backups compare against the VERY LAST backup of any type. They are very fast to create (small files), but slow to restore because you have to 'rebuild' the sequence day by day.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how a Cookie is created and used to keep you logged in.

draggableItems.content: You log into a website successfully with your password
The website server generates a small text file (cookie) with a unique session ID and sends it to your browser
Your browser saves the cookie on your hard drive
When you visit a new page on the same site, your browser sends the cookie back to prove you are already logged in

questions.explanation: Cookies act like VIP wristbands. You prove who you are once, the server gives you a wristband, and you show the wristband at every subsequent door on the site.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to attach a very large file (e.g., 5GB video) to an email.

draggableItems.content: Realize standard email cannot send files larger than 25MB
Generate a 'Shareable Link' for the uploaded file
Paste the link into the body of your email instead of attaching the file directly
Upload the 5GB video to a cloud service like Google Drive, Dropbox, or OneDrive

questions.explanation: Email protocols reject large files. You must use a third-party cloud host to store the file and use the email merely as a vehicle to deliver the access link.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how a web browser executes JavaScript.

draggableItems.content: The browser downloads the HTML and CSS to build the page structure
The browser encounters a '<script>' tag and downloads the JavaScript file
The browser's internal JavaScript engine (like V8) reads and runs the code
The running code makes the webpage interactive (e.g., opening a popup menu when you click a button)

questions.explanation: HTML is the skeleton, CSS is the skin, and JS is the muscles. JS is downloaded and executed last to add interactive behaviors to the rendered elements.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of implementing 'File Versioning' as a backup strategy.

draggableItems.content: You work on an important essay, saving it as 'Essay.docx'
You make a massive mistake and accidentally delete half the essay, then hit Save
Your cloud service automatically keeps hidden copies of previous saves (versions)
You right-click the file, select 'Version History', and restore the document to how it looked an hour ago

questions.explanation: Versioning protects you from your own mistakes. Instead of overwriting the file, the system keeps a stack of older saves you can roll back to at any time.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how an email 'Auto-Responder' works (e.g., Out of Office reply).

draggableItems.content: A client sends an email to your address
The server checks its rules and sees your 'Out of Office' setting is turned on
You configure your email server to send a specific message while you are on vacation
The server automatically sends the pre-written reply to the client on your behalf

questions.explanation: You set the rule beforehand. When mail hits the server, the server acts autonomously to reply before you ever look at your inbox.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of establishing a Virtual Private Network (VPN) connection.

draggableItems.content: The VPN server decrypts your request and fetches the webpage from the internet
You click 'Connect' in your VPN software
The software creates a secure, encrypted 'tunnel' between your computer and the VPN server
Your browser sends an encrypted request for a webpage through the tunnel

questions.explanation: A VPN acts as a secure middleman. You connect to the middleman, encrypt all traffic up to that point, and the middleman fetches the internet for you.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to restore a broken Windows computer using a 'System Restore Point'.

draggableItems.content: Select a restore point dated before the problems began
Windows reboots and reverts system files and registries to their previous state
Your personal files (documents, photos) remain untouched, but the bad driver/software is gone
Search for 'Create a restore point' in the Windows start menu and open System Restore

questions.explanation: System Restore is a time machine for OS settings, not personal files. You open the tool, pick a date, let it run, and it removes recently installed junk without deleting your essays.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how a 'Tracking Pixel' in an email works.

draggableItems.content: You open the email in your inbox
The server records the time, date, and your IP address, proving you read the email
A marketer sends you an email containing an invisible 1x1 pixel image
Your email client automatically downloads the invisible image from the marketer's server

questions.explanation: Because images are hosted on external servers, when your email app downloads the image to show it to you, the marketer's server registers that download as a 'Read Receipt'.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of resolving an IP address conflict on a home network.

draggableItems.content: Open Command Prompt and type 'ipconfig /release' to drop the conflicting IP
Your computer receives a warning: 'Another device on the network is using your IP address'
Type 'ipconfig /renew' to ask the router for a fresh, unused IP address
Your internet connection is restored with the new IP address

questions.explanation: If two computers get the same local IP, traffic crashes. You must manually force the computer to drop its current IP and ask the DHCP server (router) for a new one.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how a Content Delivery Network (CDN) speeds up web browsing.

draggableItems.content: Instead of crossing the ocean, your request is routed to the CDN server located in your own city
The website places copies of its heavy images on CDN servers distributed around the globe
You try to load a website hosted on a server in another country
The local server delivers the images in milliseconds

questions.explanation: CDNs solve the problem of physical distance. By copying files to servers all over the world, users always download data from a server physically close to them.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of properly archiving old data to free up space.

draggableItems.content: Identify large folders containing old projects you no longer need daily access to
Move those folders to a dedicated external hard drive or cold-storage cloud server
Verify the files successfully copied and open correctly from the new location
Delete the original files from your main computer's hard drive to free up space

questions.explanation: Archiving isn't backing up; it's moving. You identify cold data, move it, verify it works in the new home, and finally delete the local copy to reclaim space.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of a 'Traceroute' command (tracert) to diagnose a slow internet connection.

draggableItems.content: Open Command Prompt and type 'tracert google.com'
The command sends packets that 'hop' from router to router across the internet
Look at the list to see which specific router (hop) took the longest time to reply
It prints a list of every router it hit and how many milliseconds it took

questions.explanation: Traceroute maps the exact physical path data takes. You run the command, it tracks the hops, lists the times, and allows you to pinpoint where the bottleneck is occurring.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how 'Phishing via typosquatting' works.

draggableItems.content: The hacker registers a domain name that looks almost identical to a real one (e.g., faceboook.com)
You quickly type the URL into your browser but make a typo
The fake site loads, looking exactly like the real login page
You type your password, handing it directly to the hacker

questions.explanation: Typosquatters buy misspelled domain names, clone the real site's graphics, and wait for people to make typing mistakes to steal their credentials.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to clear the DNS Cache on a Windows PC (when a website moved but your PC still tries the old IP).

draggableItems.content: Close your web browser
Open the Start Menu, type 'cmd', and open Command Prompt
Type 'ipconfig /flushdns' and press Enter
Reopen your browser; it will now ask the internet for the site's new, updated IP address

questions.explanation: If your local DNS memory is outdated, you must flush it using the command prompt so your computer is forced to ask the internet for the updated address.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of using the 'Recycle Bin' / 'Trash' properly.

draggableItems.content: The file is moved to the Recycle Bin (but still takes up hard drive space)
Right-click the Recycle Bin and select 'Empty Recycle Bin'
Select a file and press the 'Delete' key
The OS marks the hard drive space as available, permanently erasing the file

questions.explanation: Deleting a file just moves it to a holding area. You must empty the bin to actually reclaim the storage space on the hard drive.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of a 'Denial of Service' (DDoS) attack on a web server.

draggableItems.content: The hacker commands a 'botnet' of thousands of infected computers
All computers in the botnet send fake traffic to one specific website at the exact same time
The website's server becomes overwhelmed trying to answer all the fake requests
Legitimate users are unable to load the website because the server has crashed

questions.explanation: DDoS is like a massive traffic jam. Hackers use infected PCs to flood a server with noise, blocking real traffic from getting through.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how a CAPTCHA works to prevent spam.

draggableItems.content: You attempt to submit a form on a website
The website presents a puzzle (like identifying crosswalks or distorted text)
You solve the puzzle, proving you have human visual processing skills
The website accepts the form, knowing it was not submitted by an automated bot

questions.explanation: CAPTCHAs interrupt form submissions with visual puzzles that are easy for humans but mathematically difficult for automated spam scripts to solve.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to back up a smartphone to the cloud (e.g., iCloud or Google One).

draggableItems.content: Ensure your phone is connected to Wi-Fi and plugged into a charger
Navigate to the Settings app and find the Backup menu
Toggle on 'Automatic Backups' and click 'Back Up Now'
Wait for the progress bar to complete as your photos and app data upload

questions.explanation: Phones usually require Wi-Fi (to save cellular data) and power (so it doesn't die mid-upload) before initiating large backups.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of connecting to a website using the Tor network (Dark Web routing).

draggableItems.content: Your request is bounced through three random volunteer servers around the world
The final server (exit node) fetches the website and sends it back through the maze
You open the Tor Browser and type in a web address
The website cannot tell what your original IP address is, providing anonymity

questions.explanation: Tor provides anonymity by bouncing traffic through multiple encrypted layers (nodes) so no single server knows both who you are and what site you are visiting.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of an 'Air-Gapped' backup process for extreme security.

draggableItems.content: Disconnect the external drive and put it in a physical safe
Plug a dedicated external hard drive into a secure computer
Copy highly sensitive files to the drive
Ensure the drive is NEVER connected to a computer that is connected to the internet
