questions.explanation: Air-gapping means there is literally a physical gap of air between the data and the internet. It is physically impossible for a remote hacker to access it.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how a 'Firewall' protects a home network.

draggableItems.content: The firewall inspects the data packet against its security rules
Incoming data from the internet hits your router's hardware firewall
If the data is an unrequested intrusion attempt, the firewall drops the packet entirely
If the data is a legitimate website you requested, the firewall lets it pass to your computer

questions.explanation: A firewall acts as a bouncer at a club. It stops all traffic at the door, checks it against the rules (did you invite this data in?), and blocks unsolicited traffic.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how IMAP differs from POP3 when checking email on a phone and a PC.

draggableItems.content: Using IMAP, you read and delete an email on your phone
The phone tells the central server to delete the message
Later, you open your email app on your PC
The PC syncs with the server and the email is gone from the PC as well

questions.explanation: IMAP treats the server as the master copy. Actions on one device sync back to the server and reflect on all other devices. POP3 downloads and isolates mail locally.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of 'Port Forwarding' for hosting a multiplayer game at home.

draggableItems.content: Find your computer's local IP address (e.g., 192.168.1.5)
Log into your router's admin dashboard and find the Port Forwarding section
Create a rule: 'Any traffic arriving on Port 25565 should go directly to 192.168.1.5'
Give your friends your public internet IP address so they can connect through the open port

questions.explanation: Routers block incoming traffic by default. Port forwarding tells the router 'If traffic asks for this specific door, bypass the firewall and send it to this specific computer'.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how a 'Ping' command tests a network connection.

draggableItems.content: Open Command Prompt and type 'ping 8.8.8.8'
Your computer sends a tiny packet of data (ICMP Echo Request) to that server
The server receives the packet and bounces an exact copy back to you
Your screen displays how many milliseconds the round trip took, proving the connection works

questions.explanation: Ping is sonar for computers. You send a pulse, wait for it to bounce back, and measure the time it took to confirm the target is online and reachable.

questions.question: Arrange the steps to recover a corrupted Word document from a Windows 'Shadow Copy' (Previous Versions).

draggableItems.content: Right-click the corrupted file and select 'Properties'
Click on the 'Previous Versions' tab
Select a version of the file from earlier in the day
Click 'Restore' to overwrite the corrupted file with the healthy older version

questions.explanation: Windows automatically takes hidden snapshots of files. If a file corrupts, you can use file properties to access these hidden backups and roll back.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of how a dynamic IP address is assigned via DHCP.

draggableItems.content: You turn on your laptop and it connects to the Wi-Fi router
Your laptop broadcasts a message asking, 'Does anyone have an IP address I can use?'
The router's DHCP server replies, 'Yes, you can lease 192.168.1.10 for 24 hours'
The laptop accepts the address and begins using it to access the network

questions.explanation: DHCP acts as a landlord. When a device joins, it asks for an address, the router leases it one temporarily, and the device uses it until the lease expires.

questions.question: Arrange the steps of the 'HTTPS Warning' when a website's security certificate is expired.

draggableItems.content: Your browser attempts to connect to a website via HTTPS
The browser inspects the site's SSL certificate and notices the expiration date has passed
The browser halts the connection and displays a large 'Your connection is not private' warning screen
You must manually click 'Advanced' and 'Proceed anyway' to take the risk and load the site

questions.explanation: Browsers strictly enforce certificate dates. If a site forgets to renew, the browser assumes the site might be compromised and blocks access to protect the user.
